world.title: MALAWI: Eucharist, Source of Unity with Christ and Community: Archbishop at Eucharistic Congress
world.desc:
Fr. Frank Mwinganyama
Thousands of Catholic faithful, priests, and religious sisters gathered at Mary Queen of All Hearts Cathedral in the Archdiocese of Blantyre, Malawi, for the Eucharistic Congress from 27th to 29th August 2026.
Launching the second Congress on Thursday, August 27, Archbishop Thomas Luke Msusa highlighted the centrality of the Eucharist in the life of Catholics. “We have gathered here to show our love for Christ, deepen our understanding of His real presence in the Eucharist, and show the world what we believe through a procession in the City.”
He continued, “The Eucharist is a mystery in which we become united with Christ, our Lord. Besides, it is also the Sacrament which makes us one community.
Before the launch, the Vicar General of the Archdiocese of Blantyre, Fr. George Buleya, explained the background of Eucharistic Congresses from the Reformation era to modern times. He pointed out that throughout the history of the Church, Eucharistic Congresses have been held to revive interest in the Holy Eucharist.
Held under the theme 'Rooted in Christ, nourished by the Eucharist and Sent for Mission', the three-day gathering was packed with special talks on various topics including: the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist; Understanding Adoration; the Eucharist and Marriage; and Rubrics for Proper Celebration of the Eucharist.
[caption id=attachment_25469 align=alignleft width=225] 0-0x0-0-0#[/caption]
The pinnacle of the Congress shall be a big Eucharistic Procession from the Cathedral of Mary Queen of all Hearts through Chipembere Highway to St. Louis Montfort Parish in the City of Blantyre.
The first Eucharistic Congress at the Archdiocese level was held in 2005. Last year, 2025, there was a national Eucharistic Congress where the Bishops resolved to hold similar events in their respective dioceses.

world.title: MALAWI: Grooming the Future Church: Prelate Urges Children to Love the Catholic Faith
world.desc:
By Luke Bisani
The Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Zomba, Rt. Rev. Alfred Mateyu Chaima, has urged children to deepen their love for the Catholic Church and remain committed to their faith amid contemporary challenges facing the Church.
Speaking on Thursday, August 27, during the official opening of the 2026 Children’s Congress in the Diocese of Zomba, Bishop Chaima said nurturing children in the Catholic faith was key to building a stronger and more vibrant Church for the future.
“As children, you need to have passion and take a keen interest in what you are taught by the Church. You should be ready to change your lives so that they are pleasing before God. Be involved in matters of the Church and respond to what God is calling you to do,” said Bishop Chaima.
The prelate further encouraged the children to protect and uphold their Catholic faith in the communities where they live, remain open to the guidance of the Holy Spirit, and become agents of positive change.
More than 400 children from parishes across the Diocese of Zomba have gathered at Zomba Catholic Secondary School, popularly known as Box 2, for the three-day congress, which runs from 20 to 22 August 2026.
The congress is being held under the theme, “Building a Strong Foundation of Faith in Children.”
The Catholic Diocese of Zomba currently has 20 parishes spread across its territory.
